name: advantaged
quote: I know how to solve this problem.
description: The sense that you have an ability to understand or influence an aspect of the shared environment more than others. This sense is based on a perception of a relative advantage in skill, characteristics, or other assets. It does not necessarily mean you feel yourself generally 'better' than others.
perceptions: I have the ability to change the environment or solve a problem.
I can do this better than many other people.

comparisons.description: 'Agency' is the lack of constraint for doing something while 'power' is the actual ability to get something done, whether it's your will or not.

A sense of being 'advantaged' often comes with being optimistic about a particular outcome, but not always. For example, if you're a star sports player, the other team may emphasize working against you.

Feeling 'advantaged' is just being aware of an asset you have, whether that's strength, smarts, or money. It's possible to be satisfied about such an advantage without thinking yourself generally superior to others. But it's also possible that you rank yourself socially higher due to a belief in the importance of that asset. If that's the case, others may view that assumption as arrogant.

variations.name: socially advantaged
variations.description: A sense that you have political influence -- having some authority to decide who's right, how different categories of people interact with other, and what the group should value.
perceptions: I have the ability to change the social environment or solve a social problem.
I can do this more effectively than many other people.

variations.name: physically advantaged
variations.description: The sense that your are more able than most to be able to shape the physical environment for the benefit of you or your social group.
perceptions: I have the ability to change the physical environment.
I can do this more effectively than many other people.

guidance.description: There are many references available for increasing your physical strength.

variations.name: mentally advantaged
variations.description: The sense that you are more able than most to be able to resolve problems in the world of ideas.
perceptions: I have the ability to resolve problems in the idea environment.
I can do this more effectively than many other people.

guidance.description: How to build your critical thinking skills in 7 steps (with examples)
Cultivating Wisdom: Ten practical strategies for personal and social development.

variations.name: average effectiveness
variations.description: We all have the ability to change our environment in small and average ways. But we tend to take everyday abilities for granted until we can't do them anymore.
perceptions: I have the ability to change the environment or solve a problem.
My ability to do this is not higher or lower than most other people.

comparisons.description: Most adults have the power to dig a hole or solve a simple math problem. But we know that our ability for these things is average so doing them does not provide much sensation. You only feel a sense of 'advantage' if you have a backhoe to dig the hole or are able to solve complex math problems. Likewise, you may feel 'disadvantaged' if your arthritis prevents you from digging a hole or a brain injury causes you to forget math.

variations.name: superiority
variations.description: The sense that you have a general advantage over another because you're a better person than they are.
perceptions: I have the ability to change the environment or solve a problem.
I can do this better than many other people.
This is because I'm a better person than they are.

guidance.description: A superiority complex is a belief that your abilities or accomplishments are somehow dramatically better than other people’s. People with a superiority complex may be condescending, smug, or mean to other people who don’t agree with them. Here’s everything you need to know about superiority complexes and how they affect people.

comparisons.description: When you feel 'superior' in some aspect that makes you an overall better person than others, they may perceive that outlook as being 'arrogant'. If you make a mistake while under the influence of this outlook, they may accuse you of having 'hubris'.

commentaries.quote: With great power comes great responsibility.

Nothing discloses real character like the use of power. It is easy for the weak to be gentle. Most people can bear adversity. But if you wish to know what a man really is, give him power. This is the supreme test. It is the glory of Lincoln that, having almost absolute power, he never abused it, except on the side of mercy.

Sometimes, idealistic people are put off the whole business of networking as something tainted by flattery and the pursuit of selfish advantage. But virtue in obscurity is rewarded only in Heaven. To succeed in this world you have to be known to people.
A person who won't read has no advantage over one who can't read.
To be an effective leader, you have to have a manipulative streak - you have to figure out the people working for you and give each tasks that will take advantage of his strength.
It's good to be the king.
